newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK MIXED.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted fairly stable in Monday's liquid market, dealers said.

With Z$1.4 billion worth of maturities flooding the system, the central Reserve Bank auctioned treasury bills amounting to Z$440 million at 22.94 percent and another auction was expected to mop up Z$700 million later in the day.
Last Friday, the Reserve Bank also held two liquidity control treasury bills sales, the first for Z$600 million at 22.61 percent and the second for Z$800 million with a 22.96 percent yield.
Meanwhile on Monday, treasury bills were being traded in the secondary market at 22.6 percent while call money was quoted at 22.5 percent from 19.
NCD bills with 30-, 60- and 90-day maturities were quoted at 24.5 and 22.75 percent (buying and selling respectively) from Friday's 25 and 20 percent.
Bankers acceptances were being bought firmer at 24 percent from 23 and sold at 22 percent, up from 21.5 percent.
Local money dealers expect the rates to trend upwards in the wake of a rise in annual inflation to 22.4 percent in April from 19.9 percent in March.

"What's keeping the rates down at the moment is the Reserve Bank rediscount rate which is still at 23.5 percent. But if inflation keeps going up then the Reserve Bank will have to bring it up," one dealer said.
